text:
sam: Proposal: tiny periodic "progress pulse" frames for long LLM streams. Goal: let gateway checkpoint visible progress and attempt resume-based retries (delta only) instead of full replays.
anna: How do we prevent duplicate tokens reaching the client when a resume is partial or rejected?
sam: Use monotonic seq + server-signed resume token. Gateway stores only last seq+token per stream. Upstream resume(token, seq) returns only new tokens if token valid. If resume fails, gateway hedges with a fresh request and uses circuit-breaker.
priya: Memory concerns at scale?
dave: Keep O(1) state per stream (last seq + small token blob). Evict after idle timeout (default 30s). Add a global streams threshold to open circuit.
anna: Transport details? gRPC needs a small control frame; HTTP chunked can carry chunk metadata.
sam: Example HTTP chunk metadata:
```:pulse-seq=204 :resume-token=eyJhbGci... :visible=1024```
ops-bot: rollout: pulse-proto flag enabled on staging (gateway-canary-2025-10-12) :rocket:
priya: Billing: pulses are metadata (no model token billing). Only generated model tokens are billed. Limit resume attempts per-stream to avoid abuse.
dave: Observability: resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_reject, resume_expiry, duplicate_detected. Surface per-route.
anna: Security: tokens HMAC-signed with runtime key, include stream-id and expiry to prevent replay.
sam: Backwards compat: opt-in header X-Pulse-Enable: 1; gateway emits pulses only if upstream advertises resume support.
priya: Next steps: add protocol appendix to RFC, perf sims (various RTTs/concurrency) and small dedicated runtime prototype. I'll own sims.
dave: +1
anna: +1
sam: Thanks, will update RFC and add telemetry dashboard plan.
